question: What cervical dilation marks the beginning of the active phase of labour according to current WHO guidelines?
explanation: Current WHO guidelines define the start of the active phase of the first stage of labour at 5 cm of cervical dilation. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h1)

question: Crossing the action line on a partograph during labour indicates which of the following?

options.B: Normal fetal descent has been successfully achieved
options.C: The patient is ready for immediate discharge
options.D: Labour is progressing at an accelerated rate

explanation: The action line sits four hours to the right of the alert line, and reaching it serves as a strict warning that active management or delivery steps must be initiated. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h1)

question: What are the three primary components evaluated when analyzing the causes of abnormal labour progression?
explanation: The classic obstetric triad governing labour progress consists of the power of contractions, the passenger, and the birth passage. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h2)

question: A patient with strong, frequent uterine contractions fails to dilate further because the fetal head is too large for the pelvis. Which element of labour is primarily affected here?
explanation: The fetus represents the passenger; if its size or presentation prevents movement through an adequate pelvis, it constitutes a passenger-related obstruction. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h2)

question: The presence of a pathological retraction ring, known as Bandl's ring, is a classic warning sign of which critical condition?
explanation: Bandl's ring forms when the upper uterine segment thickens and rises while the lower segment stretches thin, signaling extreme risk of uterine rupture. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h3)

question: A woman arrives at a rural Nigerian clinic after labouring at home for 36 hours. She exhibits tachycardia, dry lips, concentrated urine, and a high-rising contraction ring. What is the priority nursing action?

options.A: Encourage walking and stair climbing to speed up fetal descent
options.B: Administer high-dose oxytocin infusion to overcome uterine fatigue
options.C: Initiate immediate emergency medical notification and prepare for surgical intervention
options.D: Advise the patient to push forcefully during the next contraction

explanation: A patient with signs of obstructed and prolonged labour requires urgent medical escalation and surgical preparation rather than stimulation of contractions or pushing. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h3)

question: Vesicovaginal fistula (VVF), a devastating complication of prolonged obstructed labour, is primarily caused by which process?

options.A: Bacterial infection of the amniotic fluid
options.B: Ischemic necrosis of compressed soft tissues

explanation: Prolonged pressure from the fetal head against the pelvis cuts off blood supply to the intervening vaginal and bladder walls, leading to tissue death and fistula formation. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h4)

question: Why is postpartum hemorrhage a frequent consequence of prolonged labour?

options.A: The myometrium becomes exhausted and fails to contract effectively after delivery
options.B: Clotting factors are completely consumed during the early latent phase
options.C: The placenta implants abnormally deep into the myometrial wall
options.D: High oxytocin levels destroy platelets within the maternal circulation

explanation: Uterine inertia and muscular fatigue prevent the uterine muscle fibers from properly retracting around blood vessels post-delivery, resulting in atonic bleeding. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h4)

question: What is the primary reason for encouraging frequent bladder emptying or catheterization during prolonged labour?

options.A: Full bladders release hormones that stop uterine contractions
options.B: Urine retention prevents the kidneys from filtering medication
options.C: Bladder fullness directly causes immediate placental abruption
options.D: A full bladder displaces the uterus and can impede fetal descent

explanation: An overdistended bladder occupies pelvic space, interferes with normal uterine action, and blocks the downward movement of the presenting part. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h5)

question: Which maternal position should nurses discourage when managing a patient in prolonged labour?
explanation: The supine position causes the heavy gravid uterus to compress the vena cava and aorta, reducing maternal cardiac output and causing fetal hypoxia. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h5)

question: Which intervention is strictly CONTRAINDICATED when a diagnosis of cephalopelvic disproportion (CPD) has been confirmed?
explanation: Stimulating contractions with oxytocin when a mechanical obstruction prevents delivery will cause uterine rupture and catastrophic harm. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of performing an amniotomy during dysfunctional labour?

options.A: To administer local anesthesia directly to the cervix
options.B: To prevent the development of maternal gestational diabetes
options.C: To release prostaglandins and improve uterine contraction efficiency
options.D: To measure internal core body temperature accurately

explanation: Rupturing membranes releases local prostaglandins and brings the presenting part into direct contact with the cervix, strengthening labour progress. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h6)

question: What is the primary clinical function of the WHO partograph during labour management?

options.A: To provide early visual warning of abnormal labour progress
options.B: To calculate exact birth weight prior to delivery
options.C: To determine the precise blood type of the neonate
options.D: To serve as a permanent legal financial billing record

explanation: The partograph tracks cervical dilation and maternal-fetal well-being graphically, allowing clinicians to spot deviations from normal progress early. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h7)

question: Which strategy is most effective at the community level in reducing the incidence of severe prolonged labour in Nigeria?

options.A: Encouraging prolonged bed rest throughout the third trimester
options.B: Relying exclusively on herbal oxytocics administered at home
options.C: Restricting oral fluid intake during all stages of pregnancy
options.D: Promoting skilled birth attendance and early hospital referral

explanation: Educating communities to seek care from skilled birth attendants ensures timely detection of abnormalities and prevents delayed referrals. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h7)
